headline: Singapore and Indonesia team up to fight smoke haze

sources.title: Singapore and Indonesia set up a task force to combat haze from illegal burning (AP)
Singapore, Indonesia to set up joint task force to hold firms accountable for forest fires (The Straits Times via The Star)
Indonesian, Singapore foreign ministers meet amid spat over haze, gas (AFP via The Star)

chunks.text: Smoke from forest fires in Indonesia has covered parts of Southeast Asia in [[haze]], a thick, dirty cloud. Indonesia and [[neighboring]] Singapore have {{teamed up}} to fight it. On October 27, 2026, the two countries' [[foreign ministers]], who handle relations with other countries, met in Jakarta, Indonesia's capital. They agreed to {{set up}} a [[task force]], a special team for one goal. It will {{step up}} action against the companies behind the fires.

verbs.correct: To work as a group toward a goal
verbs.wrong: To share the cost of a meeting
verbs.why: Two friends team up to start a small business. Neighbors team up to clean the park every spring. Indonesia and Singapore have teamed up to fight the smoke haze.
Parents set up a club for kids who love chess. Many towns set up groups to help new families. The two countries agreed to set up a task force against the haze.

verbs.correct: To increase an effort or action
verbs.wrong: To write the rules for an action
verbs.why: Police step up patrols on busy weekends. Many schools step up safety checks after a storm. The new task force will step up action against the companies behind the fires.

chunks.text: Fires in western Indonesia are often started [[on purpose]] to [[clear land]] for farming. Many burn in [[peatland]], wet ground made of dead plants that burns easily when dry. The 2026 fires are the worst [[on record]], the Associated Press reports. Hot, dry weather from El Niño, a natural [[weather pattern]], made the fires worse. Singapore's foreign minister {{pointed out}} that El Niño is natural, but people cause the burning.

verbs.correct: To say something to make people notice it
verbs.wrong: To repeat a question to the group
verbs.why: My teacher points out small mistakes in my essays. A good friend points out problems in a kind way. Singapore's foreign minister pointed out that people cause the burning.

chunks.text: The haze has reached Singapore and Malaysia and {{shut down}} schools in nearby countries. Over the Indonesian part of Borneo, a large island, the smoke turned the sky orange. Both ministers said Indonesians suffer the most. Singapore sent [[warning letters]] to 10 Indonesian companies. Indonesia says it has {{looked into}} the fires. It has [[investigated]] or [[charged]] hundreds of people and more than 50 companies. About 71,000 workers are trying to {{put out}} the fires.

verbs.correct: To close for a period of time
verbs.wrong: To move to a new building
verbs.why: Heavy snow often shuts down schools for a day. Some small businesses shut down for a week in August. The haze has shut down schools in nearby countries.

verbs.correct: To study a problem to learn the facts
verbs.wrong: To send a warning to a company
verbs.why: The school looks into every report of bullying. Doctors look into the cause of a patient's pain. Indonesia says it has looked into the fires that caused the haze.

verbs.correct: To stop a fire from burning
verbs.wrong: To measure the smoke from a fire
verbs.why: Firefighters put out most house fires in a few minutes. Campers put out their fire with water before bed. About 71,000 workers in Indonesia are trying to put out the fires.

chunks.text: The task force will share [[evidence]] and information about where the companies' money goes. Indonesia's foreign minister said smoke can cross borders, and so can money. Singapore offered to {{hand over}} data on these companies, and Indonesia welcomed it. The task force may also {{go after}} those companies' [[property]]. The ministers also agreed on a [[hotline]], a direct phone line between top officials, to {{iron out}} [[disagreements]]. It was their first meeting since Indonesia's foreign minister {{took over}} on October 1.

verbs.correct: To give something to someone else
verbs.wrong: To delete something from a computer
verbs.why: Students hand over their phones before the test. The landlord hands over the keys on moving day. Singapore offered to hand over data on companies linked to the fires.

verbs.correct: To try to get or take something
verbs.wrong: To pay the taxes on something
verbs.why: Lawyers go after the money that people owe their clients. The bank goes after the house when a family stops paying. The task force may also go after those companies' property.

verbs.correct: To fix small problems or disagreements
verbs.wrong: To count small problems or disagreements
verbs.why: Managers iron out problems before a new product goes on sale. The couple irons out small problems by talking every night. The ministers agreed on a hotline to iron out disagreements.

verbs.correct: To start doing a job after someone else
verbs.wrong: To write a report for someone else
verbs.why: When the manager retires, her assistant takes over the job. A new teacher takes over the class after the winter break. Indonesia's foreign minister took over on October 1, 2026.

mainIdea.s: Singapore and Indonesia agreed to form a special team against the firms behind big fires in Indonesia. The smoke has closed schools and worried people across the region.
mainIdea.why: The two foreign ministers agreed to set up a task force to step up action against companies, because the haze has spread across Southeast Asia.

mainIdea.s: Indonesia and Singapore will send a joint team of firefighters to stop the fires in Indonesia. Both ministers said dry El Niño weather is the main cause of the smoke.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the task force goes after the companies behind the fires, and Singapore's minister pointed out that people cause the burning.

mainIdea.s: Thailand's rice farmers had a record harvest after heavy rains filled rivers and lakes. Officials said the extra rice will be sold to buyers in many countries in Asia.
mainIdea.why: This story is about Indonesia and Singapore setting up a task force to go after companies that start fires to clear land.

tf.s: Singapore and Indonesia have teamed up to fight the smoke haze.
tf.why: Their foreign ministers met in Jakarta and agreed to work together against the haze.

tf.s: The ministers said the haze is caused only by natural weather.
tf.why: Singapore's foreign minister pointed out that El Niño is natural, but the burning is caused by people.

tf.s: The new task force will step up action against companies behind the fires.
tf.why: The task force is a special team that will push harder against the companies that start the fires.

tf.s: The haze stayed inside Indonesia and did not reach other countries.
tf.why: The haze reached Singapore and Malaysia, and it has shut down schools in nearby countries.

tf.s: Indonesia says it has looked into the fires and charged some people.
tf.why: It says hundreds of people and more than 50 companies were investigated or charged, and some were found guilty.

tf.s: Indonesia refused Singapore's offer to share data on the companies.
tf.why: Indonesia welcomed Singapore's offer to hand over data on companies linked to the fires.

lines.text: Did you see that Singapore and Indonesia {{teamed up}} against the haze?
The smoke from the fires? I saw photos of an orange sky.
That was over the Indonesian part of Borneo. The haze has even {{shut down}} schools.
It sounds like the fires are [[out of control]]. What did the two countries agree to do?
Their foreign ministers met in Jakarta. They're going to {{set up}} a task force.
It will {{step up}} action against the companies that start the fires.
Wait, aren't the fires caused by El Niño?
Singapore's foreign minister {{pointed out}} that El Niño is natural, but people start the fires to clear land.
So how do you stop a company in another country?
[[Follow the money]]. Singapore offered to {{hand over}} data on the companies, and the task force may {{go after}} their property.
[[Sounds like a plan]]. Were the two governments on good terms?
Not always. They also agreed on a hotline to {{iron out}} disagreements.
Good. Maybe this meeting helped [[clear the air]].
Let's hope so. Both ministers said Indonesians suffer the most.
Once those 71,000 workers {{put out}} the fires, everyone can [[breathe easier]].

expressions.def: Used to say that something is too strong or fast for people to stop
ex: The small kitchen fire was soon out of control.

expressions.def: Used to say that you can find the truth by checking where money goes
ex: If you want to know who is behind it, follow the money.

expressions.def: Used to agree with an idea or plan that someone just shared
ex: Pizza at six, then a movie? Sounds like a plan.
We leave at eight and drive straight there. Sounds like a plan.

expressions.def: To talk openly so that bad feelings between people end
ex: The two friends met for lunch to clear the air.
A short talk with my boss helped clear the air.

expressions.def: To feel less worried because a problem is smaller now
ex: We can breathe easier now that the test is over.
Parents breathe easier when the roads are clear of snow.
